scope: Versioned structured delta after full-text methods, experiments, results, appendices, and limitations review. No paper system, code, dataset, or result was independently reproduced.

records.title: Wiki-Talkie: Multilingual Benchmarking of Persona-Based Agents on Real-World Discussions
records.verified_summary: A five-language Wikipedia Talk benchmark compares base role-play, explicit user profile, compressed behavioral traits, traits with rationale, and 5-20 raw comments from the same user. Raw comment history generally gives the closest population-level dialogue-act, sentiment, and text distributions, but history and summaries are not matched for information density or representation form.
records.research_methodology: Next-turn generation over 32,688 target comments with four anonymized generators; population-level behavioral fidelity is assessed with text similarity, dialogue-act distribution distance, and sentiment distribution distance.
records.overlap_with_personaslm: Directly compares history-based persona conditioning with explicit profile/behavior descriptions and separates several behavioral-fidelity signals.
records.difference_from_personaslm: It does not use a dated S/F/H factorial, current-versus-outdated value conflicts, CPU-deployed 0.8B-3B models, or a joint reliability-fidelity-cost estimand; its primary fidelity target is population-level rather than individual-level.

potential_novelty_threat.rationale: PersonaSLM cannot claim the first comparison of raw persona history with explicit profile/fact summaries or the first observation that history can improve behavioral fidelity.

limitations_relevant_to_personaslm: population fidelity does not establish individual fidelity

records.title: When History Helps and Hurts: Selective History Use across Multimodal Turns
records.verified_summary: ReTurn creates matched direct single-turn and multi-turn views that distinguish task-carrying from evidence-carrying history and vary historical agreement or current-evidence competition. Across 13 multimodal model configurations, the authors report a model-level median OpenQA decline from 93.7% direct to 72.3% conversational input; the design shows that recall and correct application of history are distinct.
records.research_methodology: Seven thousand base tasks (3,500 matched pairs) span Reconfirm, Reground, Retrieve, and Rebind operations with open-ended and multiple-choice views; frozen rules plus blinded model-based review score answers, without independent human agreement.
records.overlap_with_personaslm: Provides a controlled measurement design for when history should be used or ignored and separates base answerability from conversational degradation.
records.difference_from_personaslm: It is multimodal, not persona-conditioned, and does not study dated textual S/F/H packages, small CPU models, outdated-value adoption under persona conditioning, or Persona Fidelity.

potential_novelty_threat.rationale: PersonaSLM cannot claim that selective history use or history-induced degradation is itself new.

potential_methodological_improvements: label the identity of adopted competing values
limitations_relevant_to_personaslm: multimodal rather than textual persona dialogue
full test release not independently reproduced

records.title: Memory Echo in Single-Agent Long-Term Memory: Lifecycle Evaluation and Provenance-Guided Mitigation
records.verified_summary: Memory Echo identifies amplification when repeated retrieval and write-back create multiple traces from one historical source. The Family-Provenance-Authority framework limits each source family to one representative, makes superseded records ineligible after a verified correction, and constrains answers with authoritative evidence. On 190 fixed questions over four memory frameworks and two generators, the paper reports higher accuracy and lower old-answer adoption, with important failures when correction evidence is absent, noisy, or irrelevant.
records.research_methodology: Paired lifecycle replay contrasts once-only, read-only, and write-back histories, then applies a common correction and 30 read-only probes. It reports Echo Density, correction resistance, persistence, decision contamination, accuracy, and old-answer adoption, with question-level paired bootstrap intervals and component ablations.
records.overlap_with_personaslm: Directly covers provenance tracking, stale-history suppression after correction, authority-guided current-evidence use, and old-answer adoption.
records.difference_from_personaslm: It targets retrieval/write-back trace multiplication in external memory rather than static dated persona dialogue; it does not isolate S/F/H, Persona Fidelity, CPU-small-model constraints, explicit fact validity intervals, or uncertain provenance.

potential_novelty_threat.rationale: Broad claims to invent temporal provenance tracking, source-family deduplication, conditional stale-memory suppression, or authority/current-evidence gating are no longer defensible.

potential_methodological_improvements: source-family-aware contamination analysis when repeated traces exist
limitations_relevant_to_personaslm: answer-check benefit is mixed with memory selection
public repository omits main data and outputs

research_impact.core_empirical_opportunity: A paired shared-evidence 2^3 Style/Facts/dated-History factorial in CPU-deployed 0.8B-3B models, jointly measuring reliability, outdated-value adoption, persona fidelity, and cost, remains a testable distinction rather than a priority claim.
invalidated_broad_novelty_claims: First comparison of persona history and explicit profile conditioning
First demonstration that history can help or hurt task performance
First provenance-guided conditional suppression of stale memory
prospective_design_adaptations: Use matched direct/single-turn answerability references for future H mechanism cohorts.
Separate consistent history, outdated conflict, current-evidence competition, and history-required reverse controls.
Compare simple restatement, explicit temporal filtering, authority-only, and FPA-like baselines before a complex intervention.
Do not activate P6 until a residual PersonaSLM failure differs from repeated trace amplification and survives independent validation.
